 Russ Feingold backs $15 minimum wage in first campaign policy speech
 Aug 19, 2015 
 — 
 in News 
 The former U.S. senator lays out proposals for closing the country’s wealth gap as he winds up a 72-county tour.
 Former U.S. Sen. Russ Feingold for the first time endorsed a gradual doubling of the federal minimum wage to $15 in a speech Tuesday laying out several policies he would champion if voters return him to Washington next year.
 In a speech in Milwaukee to liberal advocacy group Citizen Action of Wisconsin, Feingold criticized incumbent Sen. Ron Johnson’s opposition to increasing the minimum wage, saying he was “disrespecting the hard work and dignity of too many working Wisconsinites.”
 “To me, this is fundamental,” Feingold said. “Low wages mean increased reliance on assistance programs, and less purchasing power for customers to buy needed goods and services locally. A living wage being able to put healthy food on the table for your family.”
 Feingold, a Democrat from Middleton, is running for the seat he lost to Johnson, R-Oshkosh, in 2010. His speech came as he completes a 72-county tour of the state this week.
 Johnson campaign spokesman Brian Reisinger didn’t respond to a request for comment on the minimum wage issue.
 The Marquette Law School Poll found in October that 57 percent of registered voters support increasing the minimum wage, compared with 38 percent who opposed.
 In addition to a higher minimum wage, Feingold also announced support for other policies aimed at closing the country’s wealth gap, including:
 Reinstating provisions of the Glass-Steagall Act, a 1930s law repealed in the late 1990s that separated the activities of commercial and investment banks.
 Allowing student loan refinancing and helping future students graduate debt-free.
 Opposing trade agreements that result in American jobs moving overseas.
